headings: Clinical Testing of Our Drug Candidates
paragraphs: Unless otherwise provided in this Annual Report, references to the "Company," "we," "us," and "our" refer to Puma Biotechnology, Inc. and our wholly owned subsidiary.

We are a biopharmaceutical company that develops and commercializes innovative products to enhance cancer care and improve treatment outcomes for patients. We are currently commercializing NERLYNX, an oral version of neratinib, for the treatment of certain HER2-positive breast cancers. Additionally, we have in-licensed, and are responsible for global development and commercialization of, alisertib. Alisertib is a selective, small-molecule inhibitor of Aurora Kinase A that is designed to disrupt mitosis leading to apoptosis of rapidly proliferating tumor cells that are dependent on Aurora Kinase A. Prior to our licensing alisertib from a subsidiary of Takeda Pharmaceutical Company Limited ("Takeda"), alisertib was tested in over 1,300 patients who were treated across 22 company-sponsored trials resulting in a large, well-characterized clinical safety database. Based on information in this database, we believe alisertib has potential application in the treatment of a range of different cancer types, including hormone receptor-positive breast cancer, triple negative breast cancer and small cell lung cancer. We intend to pursue development of alisertib initially in small cell lung cancer and hormone receptor-positive breast cancer.
The following figure provides an overview of our commercial product and drug candidates. EBC: Early breast cancer
** MBC: Metastatic breast cancer *** HRc+: Hormone receptor-positive **** NSCLC: Non-small cell lung cancer

Breast cancer is the leading cause of cancer death among women worldwide, with approximately 2.3 million new cases reported each year and more than 670,000 deaths globally per year. Up to 20% of breast cancer tumors show over-expression of the HER2 protein. Women with breast cancer that over-expresses HER2, referred to as HER2-positive breast cancer, are at greater risk for disease progression and death than women whose tumors do not over-express HER2. Therapeutic strategies have been developed to block HER2 in order to improve the treatment of this type of breast cancer. Trastuzumab, pertuzumab, lapatinib, T-DM1, fam‐trastuzumab deruxtecan and tucatinib are all drugs that are used as single agents, in combination with other drugs and in combination with chemotherapy to treat patients with HER2-positive breast cancer at various stages.

Neratinib is a potent irreversible tyrosine kinase inhibitor ("TKI") that blocks signal transduction through the epidermal growth factor receptors, HER1, HER2 and HER4. Based on pre-clinical studies and clinical trials to date, we believe that neratinib may offer an advantage over existing treatments that are used in the treatment of patients with HER2-positive breast cancer. We believe that by more potently inhibiting HER2 at a different site and acting via a mechanism different from other agents, neratinib may have therapeutic benefits in breast cancer patients who have been previously treated with these existing treatments, most notably due to its irreversible inhibition of the HER2 target enzyme.

NERLYNX, the commercial name for neratinib, is currently approved in the United States for two indications: the extended adjuvant treatment of adult patients with early stage HER2-overexpressed/amplified breast cancer following adjuvant trastuzumab-based therapy and for use in combination with capecitabine for the treatment of adult patients with advanced or metastatic HER2-positive breast cancer who have received two or more prior anti-HER2-based regimens in the metastatic setting. We also believe neratinib has potential clinical application in the treatment of several other cancers as well, including other tumor types that over-express or have a mutation in HER2 or epidermal growth factor receptor ("EGFR"), such as cervical cancer, lung cancer or other solid tumors.

We currently market NERLYNX in the United States using our direct specialty sales force consisting of approximately 35 sales specialists as of December 31, 2025. Our sales specialists are supported by an experienced sales leadership team consisting of regional managers and directors, as well as a commercial team of experienced professionals in marketing, access and reimbursement, managed markets, marketing research, commercial operations and sales force planning and management. Outside the United States, we have entered into exclusive sub-license agreements with third parties to pursue regulatory approval, if necessary, and commercialize NERLYNX, if approved. As of December 31, 2025, NERLYNX has received approval for the treatment of certain patients with extended adjuvant and/or metastatic HER2-positive breast cancer in more than 40 countries outside the United States, including the European Union ("EU"), China, Latin America, Australia, Canada, and Hong Kong. We are currently party to several sub-licenses in various regions outside the United States, including Europe (excluding Ukraine), Australia, Canada, China, Southeast Asia, Israel, South Korea, Russia and various countries and territories in Central America, South America, Africa and the Middle East.

In September 2022, we entered into an exclusive license agreement with Takeda to license the worldwide research and development and commercial rights to alisertib. Alisertib is an investigational, reversible, ATP-competitive inhibitor that is designed to be highly selective for Aurora Kinase A. Inhibition of Aurora Kinase A leads to disruption of mitotic spindle apparatus assembly, disruption of chromosome segregation, and inhibition of cell proliferation. In clinical trials to date, alisertib had shown single agent activity and activity in combination with other cancer drugs in the treatment of many different types of cancers, including hormone receptor-positive breast cancer, triple negative breast cancer, small cell lung cancer and head and neck cancer. Alisertib has also shown activity in previous clinical trials in peripheral T cell lymphoma and non-Hodgkin's lymphoma. Prior to our licensing alisertib from Takeda, the drug was tested in over 1,300 patients who were treated across 22 company-sponsored trials resulting in a large well-characterized clinical safety database.
Our goal is to become a leading provider of advanced therapies for the treatment of various forms of cancer. The following elements comprise our strategy to achieve this objective:

Successfully execute our NERLYNX commercial plan. An important near-term objective is to continue to execute our NERLYNX commercial plan by driving market penetration and duration of therapy consistent with the current NERLYNX label. We continue to focus our efforts on commercializing NERLYNX in the United States. In addition, we have entered into exclusive sub-license agreements with various parties to pursue regulatory approval, if necessary, and commercialize NERLYNX, if approved, in additional countries worldwide.

Advance the development of alisertib. We intend to pursue the development of alisertib in hormone receptor-positive breast cancer, as well as small cell lung cancer based on the prior clinical data that has been generated. We also plan to evaluate alisertib in biomarker focused populations where it has shown a higher degree of activity, such as patients with c-Myc amplification and RB1 loss/RB1 mutations, as we believe that this may provide a point of differentiation from the other drugs being developed in the treatment of these diseases.

Maximize the value of our programs by maintaining the flexibility to commercialize our drug candidates independently or through collaborative relationships with third parties. We are currently commercializing NERLYNX using a direct sales force in the United States and using sub-licensees in certain countries outside the United States. As we move additional drug candidates through development toward regulatory approval, we plan to evaluate several options for each drug candidate's commercialization strategy. These options include building upon or leveraging our own internal sales force; entering into a joint marketing partnership with another pharmaceutical or biotechnology company, whereby we jointly sell and market the product; and out-licensing our product, whereby another pharmaceutical or biotechnology company sells and markets our product and pays us a royalty on sales. Our decision may be different for each product that reaches commercialization and will be based on a number of factors including capital necessary to execute on each option, size of the market to be addressed and terms of potential offers from other pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies.

In-license or acquire additional commercial drugs and/or drug candidates and technologies in order to build a sustainable product pipeline by employing multiple therapeutic approaches and disciplined decision criteria based on clearly defined proof of principal goals. We seek to build a sustainable portfolio including commercial drugs where we can successfully leverage our existing commercial infrastructure and a product pipeline by employing multiple therapeutic approaches and by acquiring drug candidates belonging to known drug classes. In addition, we employ disciplined decision criteria to assess drug candidates. A decision by us to license a drug candidate will depend on a variety of factors, including the scientific merits of the technology; the costs of the transaction and other economic terms of the proposed license; the amount of capital required to develop the technology; and the economic potential of the drug candidate, should it be commercialized. We believe this strategy minimizes our clinical development risk and allows us to accelerate the development and potential commercialization of current and future drug candidates.

headings: Risks Related to our Financial Condition and Capital Requirements
While we have reported net income in recent years, we cannot assure that we will continue to do so and may not be able to maintain profitability.
We are currently a single product company with limited commercial sales experience.
We may not be able to successfully commercialize NERLYNX in the future.
Risks Related to the Discovery and Development of our Products and Drug Candidates
We are in the early stages of development of alisertib, and we cannot be certain that we will be successful if we seek regulatory approvals for our drug candidates.
Clinical trials are very expensive, time-consuming and difficult to design and implement.
Enrollment and retention of patients in clinical trials is an expensive and time-consuming process and could be made more difficult or rendered impossible by multiple factors outside our control.
The results of our clinical trials may not support our drug candidate claims.
Risks Related to Commercialization of our Drug Candidates
We are exposed to the risks associated with reliance on a direct sales force to commercialize NERLYNX in the United States.
Our NERLYNX commercialization efforts may fail to achieve the degree of market acceptance by patients and physicians necessary for commercial success.
paragraphs: In addition to the other information contained in this Annual Report, the following risk factors should be considered carefully in evaluating our company. Our business, financial condition, liquidity and results of operations could be materially adversely affected by any of these risks. The risks and uncertainties described below are not the only ones we face. Additional risks and uncertainties that we are unaware of, or that we currently believe are not material, may also become important factors that affect us.

We have incurred significant cumulative operating losses since our inception. While we have reported net income in recent years, including the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023, we cannot assure that we will continue to do so and will need to continue to generate significant revenue to sustain operations and successfully commercialize neratinib and develop alisertib. As of December 31, 2025, we had an accumulated deficit of approximately $1,283.8 million, outstanding indebtedness of approximately $22.5 million and cash and cash equivalents and marketable securities of approximately $97.5 million.

We expect to continue to incur significant expenses and may incur net losses in the future. Since inception, we have devoted substantially all of our resources to identifying, acquiring and developing NERLYNX and to its commercialization in the indications for which it has received regulatory approval. In September 2022, we in-licensed the development and global commercialization rights to our drug candidate, alisertib. Biopharmaceutical development is a highly speculative undertaking and involves a substantial degree of risk. While we experienced profitability in 2025, 2024 and 2023, we may incur operating losses in the future as we continue our efforts to commercialize NERLYNX in existing indications and to develop neratinib for additional indications, and as we commence development efforts for alisertib and any other drug candidates we may acquire.

In 2017, the FDA approved NERLYNX for the extended adjuvant treatment of adult patients with early stage HER2-overexpressed/amplified breast cancer following adjuvant trastuzumab-based therapy. In February 2020, NERLYNX was also approved by the FDA in combination with capecitabine for the treatment of adult patients with advanced or metastatic HER2-positive breast cancer who have received two or more prior anti-HER2-based regimens in the metastatic setting. In 2018, the EC granted a marketing authorization for NERLYNX in the EU for the extended adjuvant treatment of adult patients with early stage hormone receptor-positive HER2-overexpressed/amplified breast cancer and who completed adjuvant trastuzumab-based therapy less than one year ago. paragraphs: Product revenue, net consists of revenue from sales of NERLYNX. We sell NERLYNX to a limited number of specialty pharmacies and specialty distributors in the United States. We record revenue at the net sales price, which includes an estimate for variable consideration for which reserves are established. Variable consideration consists of trade discounts and allowances, product returns, provider chargebacks and discounts, government rebates and other incentives.
Product revenue also consists of product sales under sub-license agreements to our sub-licensees, who then sell into their respective international territories.
License revenue consists of consideration earned for performance obligations satisfied pursuant to our sub-license agreements.
Royalty revenue consists of consideration earned related to product sales made by our sub-licensees in their respective territories pursuant to our sub-license agreements.

Cost of sales consists of third-party manufacturing costs, freight, and indirect overhead costs associated with sales of NERLYNX. Cost of product sales also includes period costs related to royalty charges payable to Pfizer, the amortization of milestone payments made under our license agreement with Pfizer, certain inventory manufacturing services, inventory adjustment charges, unabsorbed manufacturing and overhead costs, and manufacturing variances. Cost of sales includes applicable license termination fees.
Selling, general and administrative expenses

Selling, general and administrative expenses ("SG&A expenses"), consist primarily of salaries and payroll-related costs, stock-based compensation expense, professional fees, business insurance, rent, general legal activities, credit loss expense and other corporate expenses. We expense SG&A expenses as they are incurred.

Research and development expenses ("R&D expenses") include costs associated with services provided by consultants who conduct and perform clinical services on our behalf and contract organizations for the manufacturing of clinical materials. During the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023, our R&D expenses consisted primarily of CRO fees, manufacturing of clinical materials, fees paid to consultants, salaries and related personnel costs and stock-based compensation. We expense our R&D expenses as they are incurred. Internal R&D expenses primarily consist of payroll-related costs and also include equipment costs, travel expenses and supplies. We expect R&D expenses to increase in 2026 as we expand the development of alisertib.

paragraphs: 除非本年度報告另有說明，否則提及「本公司」、「我們」、「我們」及「我們」均指 Puma Biotechnology, Inc. 及我們的 wholly owned subsidiary。

我們是一家生物製藥公司，致力於開發與商業化創新產品，以提升癌症治療與改善患者的治療結果。我們目前正商業化 NERLYNX，這是一種口服形式的 neratinib，用於治療某些 HER2-positive 乳癌。此外，我們已取得授權，並負責全球開發與商業化 alisertib。alisertib 是一種選擇性、小分子 Aurora Kinase A 抑製劑，設計用以幹擾有絲分裂，導致依賴 Aurora Kinase A 的快速增殖腫瘤細胞發生細胞凋亡。在取得 alisertib 的授權前，alisertib 已在超過 1,300 名患者身上進行測試，這些患者參與了 22 個公司贊助的試驗，產生了一個大型且特性明確的臨牀安全性資料庫。根據此資料庫的資訊，我們認為 alisertib 有潛在應用於治療多種不同癌症類型的可能，包括荷爾蒙受體陽性乳癌、三陰性乳癌及小細胞肺腺癌。我們計畫首先在小細胞肺腺癌及荷爾蒙受體陽性乳癌中進行 alisertib 的開發。
下圖提供我們商業產品與藥物候選品的概覽。EBC: 早期乳癌
** MBC: 轉移性乳癌 *** HRc+: 荷爾蒙受體陽性 **** NSCLC: 非小細胞肺腺癌

乳癌是全球女性癌症死亡的主要原因，每年約有 2.3 百萬新病例被報告，且全球每年有超過 670,000 名女性死於乳癌。約有 20% 的乳癌腫瘤顯示 HER2 蛋白過度表現。患有 HER2 蛋白過度表現乳癌的女性，被稱為 HER2-positive 乳癌，其疾病惡化與死亡風險較那些腫瘤未過度表現 HER2 的女性更高。已發展出治療策略以阻斷 HER2，以改善此類乳癌的治療。Trastuzumab、pertuzumab、lapatinib、T-DM1、fam-trastuzumab deruxtecan 及 tucatinib 都是用於治療不同階段 HER2-positive 乳癌患者的藥物，可作為單一藥物、與其他藥物合用，或與化療合用。

Neratinib 是一種強效不可逆的酪胺酸 kinase 抑製劑（"TKI"），會阻斷經表皮生長因子受體（HER1、HER2 和 HER4）傳導的訊號。根據目前的臨牀前研究與臨牀試驗，我們認為 neratinib 可能比目前用於治療 HER2-positive 乳癌患者的現有治療方式更具優勢。我們認為，透過更強效地在不同位點抑制 HER2 並透過與其他藥物不同的機製作用，neratinib 可能在曾接受這些現有治療方式的乳癌患者中提供治療效益。

NERLYNX 是 neratinib 的商業名稱，目前在美國已核准兩項適應症：用於早期階段 HER2-overexpressed/amplified 乳癌患者，在接受 adjuvant trastuzumab 基礎治療後的延長輔助治療，以及與 capecitabine 合併使用，用於治療已接受兩次或以上 anti-HER2 基礎治療的晚期或轉移性 HER2-positive 乳癌患者。我們也認為 neratinib 有潛在的臨牀應用於治療其他癌症，包括過度表現或有 HER2 或表皮生長因子受體（"EGFR"）突變的其他腫瘤類型，例如子宮頸癌、肺癌或其他實體瘤。

我們目前在美國市場銷售 NERLYNX，使用我們的直接專門銷售團隊，截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，約有 35 名銷售專員。我們的銷售專員由經驗豐富的銷售領導團隊支持，該團隊包括區域經理與總監，以及在市場行銷、門檻准入與報銷、管理市場、市場研究、商業運作及銷售團隊規劃與管理方面有經驗的專業人員。在美國以外的地區，我們已與第三方簽訂獨家次授權協議，以追求必要的監管核准，並商業化 NERLYNX，若核准後。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，NERLYNX 已在美國以外的超過 40 個國家獲得核准，用於治療某些患者，包括在擴展輔助及/或轉移性 HER2-positive 乳癌的治療，這些國家包括歐盟（"EU"）、中國、拉丁美洲、澳洲、加拿大及香港。我們目前在美國以外的多個地區擁有幾個次授權協議，包括歐洲（不包括烏克蘭）、澳洲、加拿大、中國、東南亞、以色列、韓國、俄羅斯以及中美洲、南美洲、非洲和中東的多個國家和地區。

2022年9月，本公司與Takeda簽訂獨家授權協議，授權本公司取得alisertib在全球的研究與開發及商業化權利。alisertib為一種正在研究中的可逆性、ATP競爭性抑制劑，設計上具備高度選擇性針對Aurora Kinase A。抑制Aurora Kinase A會導致有絲分裂紡錘體裝置組裝受擾、染色體分離受擾，以及細胞增殖受抑制。根據目前臨牀試驗的結果，alisertib在治療多種不同類型癌症，包括荷爾蒙受體陽性乳癌、三陰性乳癌、小細胞肺腺癌及頭頸癌時，已顯示單獨使用或與其他抗癌藥物合用時的療效。alisertib在過去的臨牀試驗中也顯示對周邊T細胞淋巴瘤及非霍奇金氏淋巴瘤的療效。在本公司取得alisertib的授權前，該藥物已在超過1,300名患者身上進行試驗，這些患者參與了22項由本公司贊助的試驗，形成一個規模龐大且特性明確的臨牀安全性資料庫。
本公司目標成為治療各種癌症形式的先進療法領導供應商。以下為本公司達成此目標的策略要素：
成功執行NERLYNX商業計畫。一個重要的短期目標是持續執行NERLYNX商業計畫，推動市場滲透率與治療持續時間，符合目前NERLYNX標籤的標準。本公司持續專注於美國NERLYNX的商業化。此外，本公司已與各項當事人簽訂獨家次授權協議，以追求必要的監管批准，並在獲得批准後，於全球其他國家進行NERLYNX的商業化。
推進alisertib的開發。本公司有意根據已產生的臨牀資料，針對荷爾蒙受體陽性乳癌以及小細胞肺腺癌進行alisertib的開發。本公司也計畫評估alisertib在具有更高療效表現的生物標記聚焦族羣，例如具有c-Myc擴增及RB1喪失/RB1突變的患者，因為本公司認為這可能提供與治療這些疾病其他藥物不同的優勢。

透過獨立商業化或與第三方合作關係，最大化本公司計畫的價值。目前本公司在美國透過直接銷售團隊商業化NERLYNX，並在美國以外的部分國家透過次授權方進行商業化。當本公司將更多藥物候選品推進至開發階段並獲得監管批准時，本公司計畫評估每個藥物候選品的商業化策略選項。這些選項包括延續或利用本公司內部銷售團隊；與另一家製藥或生物科技公司建立共同行銷合作關係，共同銷售與行銷該產品；以及出授權，讓另一家製藥或生物科技公司銷售與行銷本公司產品並支付銷售 royalty。本公司對每個產品的商業化決策可能不同，並根據多種因素，包括執行每個選項所需的資金、所要面對的市場規模，以及來自其他製藥和生物科技公司的潛在合作提案條款。

進口或取得額外的商業化藥物及/或藥物候選品與技術，以透過多種治療方法與嚴謹的決策標準，根據明確界定的證據原則目標，建立可持續的產品管道。本公司尋求建立可持續的產品組合，包括可成功利用本公司現有商業基礎設施的商業化藥物，以及透過多種治療方法與取得屬於已知藥物類別的藥物候選品的產品管道。此外，本公司運用嚴謹的決策標準評估藥物候選品。本公司決定授權某藥物候選品，將根據多種因素，包括技術的科學價值；交易成本及其他提出的授權條款；開發該技術所需的資金；以及該藥物候選品若商業化後的經濟潛力。本公司認為此策略可降低本公司臨牀開發風險，並允許本公司加速目前及未來藥物候選品的開發與潛在商業化。

paragraphs: 產品營業收入，淨額包含來自NERLYNX銷售的營業收入。我們將NERLYNX銷售給美國極少數的專門藥房及專門分銷商。我們在淨銷售價格確認收入，此價格包含變動對價的預估，並建立備抵積累。變動對價包含貿易折扣與允許減讓、產品退回、提供者退費與折扣、政府補貼及其他激勵措施。
產品營業收入也包含根據我們的次授權協議，向次授權人銷售產品，然後由次授權人銷售至其各自國際地區的產品銷售。
授權收入包含因履行我們次授權協議中的績效義務而獲得的對價。
版稅收入包含因根據我們的次授權協議，次授權人在其各自地區銷售產品而獲得的對價。
銷售成本包含第三方製造成本、運費及與NERLYNX銷售相關的間接過頭費用。產品銷售成本也包含與支付給輝瑞的版稅費用相關的期間費用、根據我們與輝瑞的授權協議支付的里程碑付款的攤銷費用、某些存貨製造服務、存貨調整費用、未吸收製造及過頭費用及製造變動。銷售成本包含適用的授權終止費用。
銷售及一般行政費用
銷售及一般行政費用（"SG&A費用"），主要包含薪資及與薪資相關的成本、股票基於報酬費用、專業費用、商業保險、租金、一般法律活動、信用減損費用及其他公司費用。我們在發生時將SG&A費用費用化。

研究與開發費用（"R&D費用"）包含與由顧問提供服務的成本，這些顧問代表我們執行及進行臨牀服務，以及合同組織製造臨牀材料的成本。在截至2025年12月31日、2024年及2023年的會計年度，我們的R&D費用主要包含CRO費用、臨牀材料製造費用、支付給顧問的費用、薪資及相關人員費用和股票基於報酬費用。我們在發生時將R&D費用費用化。內部R&D費用主要包含與薪資相關的成本，也包含設備費用、差旅費用及辦公用品費用。我們預期2026年的R&D費用將因我們擴展alisertib的開發而增加。

headings: 與本公司財務狀況及資金需求相關之風險
雖然我們在近年內已報告有淨收入，但我們無法保證將持續如此，且可能無法維持獲利能力。
目前本公司為單一產品公司，且商業銷售經驗有限。
我們可能無法成功商業化NERLYNX。
與本公司產品及藥物候選品之發現與開發相關之風險
我們目前處於alisertib之開發初期階段，若我們尋求對藥物候選品之監管批准，我們無法確定是否能成功。
臨牀試驗非常昂貴、耗時且難以設計與執行。
臨牀試驗中之受試者招募與留存為一昂貴且耗時的過程，且可能因多項超出我們控制範圍之因素而變得更加困難或無法進行。
我們臨牀試驗的結果可能無法支持我們的藥物候選品聲稱的療效。
與我們藥物候選品商業化相關的風險
我們面臨因依賴直接銷售團隊來美國市場推廣NERLYNX而產生的風險。
我們的NERLYNX商業化努力可能無法達到患者與醫生所需的市場接受度，以實現商業成功。
paragraphs: 除本年度報告中包含的其他資訊外，下列風險因素應謹慎考量，以評估本公司。本公司業務、財務狀況、流動性及營運成果可能因任何上述風險而受到重大不利影響。下列所述的風險與不確定性並非本公司所面臨的唯一風險。此外，我們可能還會面臨其他我們未察覺或目前認為不具重大性的風險與不確定性，這些也可能成為影響我們的重要因素。

本公司自設立以來已產生顯著累計營運虧損。雖然本公司在近年間，包括2025年12月31日、2024年12月31日及2023年12月31日結帳年度，已報導淨收入，但本公司無法保證將持續如此，並需持續產生顯著收入以維持營運並成功商業化neratinib及開發alisertib。截至2025年12月31日，本公司累計虧損約為1,283.8 百萬美元，未償還債務約為22.5 百萬美元，以及現金及現金等價物與市場可交易證券約為97.5 百萬美元。

我們預期將持續產生顯著費用，並可能在未來產生淨虧損。自成立以來，我們已將 substantially all 的資源投入於識別、取得及發展NERLYNX，並於其已獲得監管核准的適應症中進行商業化。2022年9月，我們取得藥物候選品alisertib的開發與全球商業化權利。生物製藥的開發是一項高度投機的業務，並涉及相當程度的風險。雖然我們在2025年、2024年及2023年實現了獲利，但我們可能在未來因持續努力於NERLYNX在現有適應症中的商業化，以及發展neratinib用於其他適應症，以及啟動alisertib及其他可能取得的藥物候選品的開發而產生營運虧損。

2017年，美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）核准NERLYNX用於治療完成輔助曲妥珠單抗治療後的早期階段HER2過表達/擴增乳癌成人患者之延長輔助治療。2020年2月，NERLYNX亦被FDA核准與卡培他濱聯合使用，用於治療已接受兩種或以上前線抗HER2治療方案的晚期或轉移性HER2陽性乳癌成人患者。2018年，歐盟委員會（EC）核准NERLYNX在歐盟用於治療完成輔助曲妥珠單抗治療不足一年的早期階段荷爾蒙受體陽性HER2過表達/擴增乳癌成人患者之延長輔助治療。我們也正在alisertib的早期開發階段。任何藥物候選品的成功開發與商業化，將需要我們執行多種功能，包括：
進行預臨牀開發與臨牀試驗；參與監管核准程序；
製備與製造產品；成功進行銷售與行銷活動；以及
